hindi: अब इसके बाद हम विधिशोणितीय अध्याय की व्याख्या करेंगे।
english: Now, therefore, we shall expound the chapter on blood and regimen (Vidhiśoṇitīya).
notes: The chapter name Vidhiśoṇitīya is a derived title word and is not split; it takes up vidhinā śoṇitam of unit 3.

hindi: ऐसा भगवान् आत्रेय ने कहा।
english: Thus said the venerable Ātreya.

words.gloss: of place, time and habitual suitability
words.gram: n. gen. pl., dvandva (okas-sātmya = habitual suitability)
m. nom. sg., ppp. caus. sam-pra-√kāś

hindi: देहधारियों का रक्त विधि से उत्पन्न होने पर शुद्ध होता है, वह विधि जो देश, काल और ओकसात्म्य के विषय में बताई गई है।
english: In embodied beings, blood produced by following the regimen (vidhi) is pure, the regimen of place, time and habitual suitability (okasātmya) that has been set forth.
notes: okasātmya (printed kāla + okas giving kālaukas) = habitual suitability, the okaḥsātmya of the glossary. The relative clause defines which vidhi is meant; the text does not say here where it was set forth.

words.gloss: with strength, complexion, happiness and life-span

hindi: क्योंकि वह शुद्ध रक्त प्राणियों को बल, वर्ण, सुख और आयु से युक्त करता है; क्योंकि (जीवन) रक्त का अनुसरण करता है।
english: For that pure blood endows living beings with strength, complexion, happiness and life-span; for (life) follows the blood.

text_flags.suggest: (a two-syllable word appears to be missing)
text_flags.why: metre: this half-verse line has 14 syllables instead of 16, and anuvartate has no expressed subject; the missing word cannot be restored from the chunk

notes: The second half-line is two syllables short and anuvartate (3 sg.) lacks a subject; '(life)' in the translations is supplied from āyuṣā of the first line and is only a stopgap. prāṇinaḥ is taken as acc. pl. object of yunakti.

words.gloss: spoiled, (taken) in excess, sharp and hot

words.gram: m. inst. pl., dvandva with ati-

hindi: बिगड़े हुए, अधिक मात्रा वाले, तीक्ष्ण और उष्ण मद्यों से और उसी प्रकार के अन्य (पेयों) से; उसी तरह अति लवण और क्षार से, अम्ल से और कटु पदार्थों से भी;
english: By wines that are spoiled, (taken) in excess, sharp and hot, and by other (drinks) of that kind; likewise by excess of salt and alkalis (kṣāra), by sour things and by pungent things too;

text_flags.why: vidhra is not a word; tad-vidha 'of that kind' (inst. pl. tadvidhaiḥ) fits the grammar and sense, agreeing with anyaiḥ; the extra r adds no syllable

notes: The sentence (list of causes) runs on through unit 10, where the verb śoṇitaṃ saṃpraduṣyati comes. bahu is taken as 'in excess'; it could also mean simply 'much, abundant'. ati- is taken to govern both lavaṇa and kṣāra.

words.gloss: by use of kulattha, māṣa, niṣpāva and sesame oil
words.gram: n. inst. pl., tat-puruṣa with inner dvandva

words.gloss: of piṇḍālu, mūlaka and the like

hindi: कुलत्थ, माष, निष्पाव और तिल के तेल के सेवन से; पिण्डालु, मूलक आदि सब प्रकार के हरे शाकों के (सेवन से),
english: by the use of kulattha, māṣa, niṣpāva and sesame oil; by (the use) of piṇḍālu, mūlaka and other green vegetables of all kinds,
notes: The genitives of line 2 depend on sevanāt in unit 7. Identifications: kulattha = horse gram, Macrotyloma uniflorum (standard); māṣa = black gram, Vigna mungo (standard); niṣpāva = Lablab purpureus (probable); piṇḍālu = a yam, Dioscorea sp. (probable); mūlaka = radish, Raphanus sativus (standard). sarvaśaḥ could also mean 'in every way, entirely'.

words.gloss: of the prasaha (animals that seize by force)
of curd, sour things, whey and śukta

hindi: जलज, आनूप और बिलवासी प्राणियों के तथा प्रसह प्राणियों के (मांस के) सेवन से; दही, अम्ल पदार्थ, मस्तु और शुक्त के तथा सुरा और सौवीरक के (सेवन से);
english: from the use (of the flesh) of water-born, marsh and burrow-dwelling animals and of the prasaha (animals that seize by force); (from the use) of curd, sour things, whey (mastu) and śukta, and of surā and sauvīraka;

text_flags.why: possible: sukta gives no sense in a list of curd preparations and sour drinks; śukta (a fermented sour preparation) fits; s for ś changes no syllable

notes: 'Flesh' is understood: the text names only the animal groups. baila (from bila 'burrow') = burrow-dwellers. amla is taken as a separate member 'sour things'; it could also qualify mastu ('sour whey'). surā, sauvīraka and śukta are kept in Sanskrit.

words.gram: m. gen. pl., pres. part. pra-√svap

hindi: विरुद्ध, सड़े-गले और दुर्गन्धित पदार्थों के भक्षण से; और द्रव, स्निग्ध और गुरु पदार्थ खाकर दिन में सोने वालों का;
english: by eating incompatible, decomposed and putrid things; and of those who sleep by day after eating liquid, unctuous and heavy things;
notes: upaklinna literally 'moistened through, soaked', here taken as decomposed. The genitive prasvapatām ('of those who...') continues in unit 9 (bhajatām) and goes with śoṇitaṃ saṃpraduṣyati of unit 10 ('the blood of those who ...').

words.gloss: from suppression of the urge to vomit

hindi: अति आदान, उसी प्रकार क्रोध, और धूप तथा अग्नि का सेवन करने वालों का; छर्दि के वेग को रोकने से, और समय पर रक्त न निकालने से;
english: of those who resort to excessive intake, likewise to anger, and to the sun and fire; from suppressing the urge to vomit, and from not letting blood at the (proper) time;

text_flags.why: atyādānāṃ is not a form of atyādāna (gen. pl. would be atyādānānām); the acc. sg. atyādānam, object of bhajatām like krodham, fits the grammar; same syllable count

notes: atyādāna literally 'excessive taking (in)', taken as excessive intake (of food); the text does not say of what. avasecana = letting out of blood; anavasecana is its absence.

words.gloss: by indigestion and eating on top of undigested food
from the nature of the Śarad season

hindi: श्रम, अभिघात और संताप से, उसी प्रकार अजीर्ण और अध्यशन से, और शरद् काल के स्वभाव से रक्त दूषित हो जाता है।
english: By fatigue, injury and heat, likewise by indigestion (ajīrṇa) and eating on top of undigested food (adhyaśana), and from the nature of the Śarad season, the blood becomes vitiated.
notes: This verb closes the list of causes begun in unit 5. saṃtāpa taken as heat (exposure, burning); it could also mean distress. Śarad is roughly autumn (season equivalent).

words.gloss: putrid odour of nose and mouth

hindi: तब रक्त से उत्पन्न अनेक प्रकार के रोग उत्पन्न होते हैं: मुखपाक, आँखों की लालिमा, नाक और मुख की सड़ी गन्ध,
english: Then diseases born of blood, of various kinds, arise: mukhapāka (inflammation of the mouth), redness of the eyes, putrid odour of the nose and mouth,
notes: The list of blood-born diseases runs through unit 16. pāka literally 'cooking, ripening', i.e. inflammation or suppuration.

words.gloss: gulma, upakuśa, vīsarpa, raktapitta and pramīlaka

hindi: गुल्म, उपकुश, वीसर्प, रक्तपित्त, प्रमीलक, विद्रधि, रक्तमेह, प्रदर, वातशोणित,
english: gulma, upakuśa, vīsarpa, raktapitta, pramīlaka, vidradhi (abscess), raktameha, pradara, vātaśoṇita,
notes: Disease names kept in Sanskrit with no identifications. upakuśa and pramīlaka are given no gloss beyond the name.

words.gram: f. nom. sg., abstract of bahuvrīhi

hindi: विवर्णता, अग्नि की मन्दता, प्यास, शरीर का भारीपन, संताप, अति दुर्बलता, अरुचि और सिर का दर्द,
english: discoloration, weakness of the digestive fire (agni), thirst, heaviness of the body, burning heat, extreme weakness, loss of taste (aruci) and pain in the head,

words.gram: n. nom. sg., tat-puruṣa with inner dvandva
f. nom. sg., abstract of bahuvrīhi

hindi: अन्न-पान का विदाह, तिक्त और अम्ल उद्गार, क्लम, क्रोध की अधिकता, बुद्धि का संमोह, मुख का खारापन,
english: burning (vidāha) of food and drink, bitter and sour belching, exhaustion (klama), abundance of anger, confusion of the intellect, saltiness in the mouth,
notes: buddheḥ is taken with saṃmohaḥ ('confusion of the intellect'); it could also be read with krodhapracuratā ('the intellect's abundance of anger'). vidāha of food = burning during digestion.

words.gram: m. nom. sg., tat-puruṣa with inner dvandva

hindi: स्वेद, शरीर की दुर्गन्ध, मद, कम्प, स्वर का क्षय, तन्द्रा और निद्रा की अधिकता, और अन्धकार का अधिक दिखना,
english: sweating, foul smell of the body, intoxication (mada), tremor, loss of voice, excess of drowsiness and sleep, and excessive seeing of darkness,
notes: daurgandhya (dur- 'bad' + gandha) is printed, hence 'foul smell'. tamaso 'tidarśanam: seeing darkness in excess, i.e. frequent blackouts of vision; literal rendering kept.

words.gloss: itching, arus, koṭha, eruptions, kuṣṭha, carmadala and the like
words.gram: m. nom. pl., bahuvrīhi with inner dvandva

hindi: कण्डू, अरुः, कोठ, पिडका, कुष्ठ, चर्मदल आदि; ये सभी विकार रक्त पर आश्रित जानने चाहिए।
english: itching (kaṇḍū), arus, koṭha, eruptions (piḍakā), kuṣṭha, carmadala and the like: all these disorders are to be known as based on blood.
notes: arus (in compound aruḥ), koṭha, kuṣṭha and carmadala kept in Sanskrit; literal sense of arus 'sore', of carmadala 'splitting of the skin'. sarva (printed) is sarve with the e dropped before eva in sandhi, as is regular.

words.gloss: with cold, hot, unctuous, dry and other (measures)
words.gram: n. inst. pl., bahuvrīhi with inner dvandva

hindi: जो रोग साध्य हों और शीत, उष्ण, स्निग्ध, रूक्ष आदि उपायों से ठीक प्रकार चिकित्सित किए जाने पर सिद्ध न हों, उन्हें रक्तज समझना चाहिए।
english: Those diseases which, though curable and properly treated with cold, hot, unctuous, dry and other (measures), are not cured, one should recognise as born of blood.
notes: samyak is taken with upakrāntāḥ ('properly treated'); it could also go with sādhyāḥ ('fully curable'). The ca after upakrāntāḥ is read as concessive ('though').

hindi: रक्त के रोगों में रक्तपित्त को दूर करने वाली चिकित्सा करनी चाहिए, तथा विरेक, उपवास और रक्त का स्रावण।
english: In diseases of the blood one should carry out the treatment that removes raktapitta, and purgation, fasting and letting out of blood.

words.gloss: according to the measure of strength and doṣa
words.gram: n. abl. sg., tat-puruṣa with inner dvandva

hindi: बल और दोष के प्रमाण के अनुसार, या रक्त की शुद्धि (के आधार) से, या आशय को भली भाँति देखकर, मनुष्य का रक्त निकालना चाहिए।
english: One should let out the person's blood either according to the measure of strength and doṣa, or by (the standard of) the purity of the blood, or having carefully examined the āśaya (site).
notes: viśuddhyā rudhirasya is taken as 'until the blood (flows) pure', i.e. purity as the limit; the text gives only the instrumental. āśaya kept in Sanskrit ('site, reservoir'); the text does not say which site is meant.

hindi: वात से (दूषित रक्त) अरुण आभा वाला, विशद, झागदार और पतला होता है; पित्त से रक्त पीला और काला होता है और उष्णता के कारण देर से जमता है।
english: (Blood vitiated) by Vāta is reddish in appearance, non-slimy, frothy and thin; by Pitta the blood is yellow and dark and, because of heat, clots slowly.
notes: duṣṭam of unit 21 ('vitiated') is understood here. pītāsita can be read 'yellow and dark' or 'yellowish-dark'.

words.gloss: with the signs of all three

hindi: कफ से दूषित (रक्त) थोड़ा पाण्डु, पिच्छिल, तन्तुयुक्त और घन होता है; संसर्ग से मिले-जुले लक्षणों वाला, और सान्निपातिक तीनों के लक्षणों वाला होता है।
english: Vitiated by Kapha, it is slightly pale, slimy, stringy and compact; from a combination (of two doṣas) it has combined signs, and from all three together (sānnipātika) it has the signs of all three.
notes: tantumat literally 'having threads'. saṃsarga is taken as the combination of two doṣas, contrasted with sānnipātika (all three); the text does not say 'two'.

words.gloss: with the lustre of gold and of the indragopa
words.gram: n. acc. sg., bahuvrīhi with inner dvandva
n. acc. sg., bahuvrīhi with inner dvandva

words.gloss: of the colour of the guñjā fruit

hindi: तपाए हुए सोने और इन्द्रगोप की आभा वाले, कमल और अलक्तक के समान, और गुञ्जा फल के समान रंग वाले रक्त को शुद्ध जानो।
english: Know as pure the blood that has the lustre of refined gold (tapanīya) and of the indragopa, that resembles the lotus and lac-dye (alaktaka), and that has the colour of the guñjā fruit.
notes: tapanīya = gold (literally 'to be heated', i.e. refined gold). indragopa kept in Sanskrit (a creature; no identification). Identification: guñjā = Abrus precatorius (standard).

words.gram: n. nom. sg., dvandva (adjectival) with ati-

hindi: रक्त निकाल दिए जाने पर ऐसा अन्न-पान हितकर है जो न अधिक उष्ण हो न अधिक शीतल, लघु और दीपन हो; क्योंकि तब शरीर अस्थिर रक्त वाला होता है, और अग्नि की विशेष रूप से रक्षा करनी चाहिए।
english: When the blood has been let out, food and drink that is neither too hot nor too cold, light and stimulating to digestion is beneficial; for then the body has unsteady blood, and the digestive fire (agni) is to be protected especially.

text_flags.why: anavastita is not a word; anavasthita 'unsteady' (an-ava-√sthā) fits the grammar and sense of a body whose blood has just been let out; t for th changes no syllable

notes: Upajāti verse (11 syllables a quarter). anavasthitāsṛk is read as a bahuvrīhi agreeing with śarīram ('having unsteady blood').

words.gloss: whose complexion and senses are clear
words.gram: m. acc. sg., bahuvrīhi with inner dvandva

words.gloss: whose digester and urges are unobstructed
words.gram: m. acc. sg., bahuvrīhi with inner dvandva
m. acc. sg., tat-puruṣa with inner dvandva

hindi: जिसका वर्ण और इन्द्रियाँ प्रसन्न हों, जो इन्द्रियों के विषयों की इच्छा करता हो, जिसका पक्ता और वेग बिना बाधा के हों, जो सुख से युक्त, तुष्टि और बल से सम्पन्न हो, ऐसे शुद्ध रक्त वाले पुरुष का वे अभिनन्दन करते हैं।
english: The man whose complexion and senses are clear, who desires the objects of the senses, whose digester (paktṛ) and urges are unobstructed, who is endowed with happiness and possessed of contentment and strength, him they hail as a man of pure blood.

text_flags.why: possible: vandanti 'they salute, praise' gives a weak sense for what is a description of signs (compare viddhi 'know' in unit 22); vadanti 'they call' fits a definition; both scan the same (11 syllables)

notes: Upajāti verse. '(puṣṭi-)' is printed in round brackets after tuṣṭibalopapannaṃ, apparently as an alternative reading puṣṭi- 'nourishment' for tuṣṭi- 'contentment'; the input does not say what the brackets mean, it is not counted in the metre, and it is not applied. paktṛ (the digester) is read with vega as a dvandva ('digester and urges'); it could also be read as a tat-puruṣa 'the force of the digester'. vandanti is kept as printed in the split and translation.

words.gram: n. acc. pl., upapada tat-puruṣa with inner dvandva

hindi: किन्तु जब कुपित मल, अलग-अलग या सब मिलकर, रक्त को वहन करने वाले और रस तथा संज्ञा को वहन करने वाले स्रोतों को
english: But when the aggravated malas, singly or all together, the channels that carry blood and those that carry rasa and consciousness (saṃjñā),
notes: The sentence continues into unit 26 (pratihatya avatiṣṭhante 'having obstructed, settle'). malāḥ (glossary: waste) are here said to be aggravated (kupita); units 28 and 29 name vāyu, Pitta and Kapha as the agents, so the malas here are the doṣas. rasa is kept in Sanskrit (here the bodily fluid, not taste).

words.gloss: of one habituated to unclean food
whose self is covered by rajas and delusion
words.gram: m. gen. sg., bahuvrīhi with inner dvandva

hindi: मलिन आहार के अभ्यस्त और रज तथा मोह से आवृत आत्मा वाले मनुष्य के, रोककर ठहर जाते हैं, तब रोग उत्पन्न होते हैं:
english: of a person habituated to unclean food, whose self is covered by rajas and delusion (moha), having obstructed (them), settle (there), then diseases arise:
notes: Continues the sentence of unit 25; the diseases are named in unit 27. rajas kept in Sanskrit (the quality of the mind).

hindi: मद, मूर्च्छाय और संन्यास। विचक्षण व्यक्ति इनके हेतु, लक्षण और उपशान्ति में उत्तरोत्तर बल की अधिकता जाने।
english: mada (intoxication), mūrcchāya (fainting) and saṃnyāsa (collapse). The discerning one should know that among these the strength increases successively in cause, signs and alleviation.
notes: mada, mūrcchāya and saṃnyāsa are kept in Sanskrit with literal glosses (saṃnyāsa literally 'laying down, abandonment'); no modern identifications. mūrcchāya is kept as printed (the masculine noun of the same root as mūrcchā). 'Strength' increases in the order given: saṃnyāsa is the strongest.

words.gram: m. nom. sg., pres. part. caus. vi-√kṣubh

hindi: जब वायु चित्त के दुर्बल स्थान में प्रवेश करता है, तब वह मनुष्य के मन को क्षुब्ध करता हुआ उसकी संज्ञा को मोहित कर देता है।
english: When Vāta (vāyu) enters the weakened seat of the mind, then, agitating the mind, it confuses the person's consciousness.
notes: jantoḥ may go with manaḥ or with saṃjñām ('the person's mind / consciousness'); the sense is the same.

words.gram: m. nom. sg., pres. part. caus. vi-√kṣubh

hindi: इसी प्रकार पित्त और इसी प्रकार कफ मनुष्यों के मन को क्षुब्ध करता हुआ संज्ञा को व्याकुलता में पहुँचा देता है; और इसमें जो भेद है वह बताया जाएगा।
english: In the same way Pitta, and likewise Kapha, agitating the mind of men, brings consciousness into confusion; and the distinction here will be stated.
notes: vikṣobhayan and nayati are singular, applying to Pitta and Kapha each in turn. The distinction is given from unit 30 on.

words.gloss: whose speech is halting, profuse and hurried
words.gram: m. acc. sg., bahuvrīhi with inner dvandva

words.gloss: whose movements are unsteady and stumbling
words.gram: m. acc. sg., bahuvrīhi with inner dvandva

words.gloss: whose appearance is dry, dusky and reddish
words.gram: m. acc. sg., bahuvrīhi with inner dvandva

hindi: जिसकी वाणी अटकती हुई, अधिक और तेज़ हो, जिसकी चेष्टाएँ चंचल और लड़खड़ाती हुई हों, और जिसकी आकृति रूक्ष, श्याव और अरुण हो, उसे वात के मद से ग्रस्त जानना चाहिए।
english: One whose speech is halting, profuse and hurried, whose movements are unsteady and stumbling, and whose appearance is dry, dusky and reddish, one should know to be seized by the mada of Vāta.
notes: sakta literally 'stuck, clinging', taken as halting speech. śyāva = dusky, dark-brownish.

words.gloss: whose speech is angry and harsh

words.gloss: whose appearance is red, yellow or dark
words.gram: m. acc. sg., bahuvrīhi with inner dvandva

hindi: जिसकी वाणी क्रोधयुक्त और कठोर हो, जिसे मार-पीट और कलह प्रिय हो, और जिसकी आकृति लाल, पीली या काली हो, उसे पित्त के मद से ग्रस्त जानना चाहिए।
english: One whose speech is angry and harsh, who is fond of fighting and quarrels, and whose appearance is red, yellow or dark, one should know to be seized by the mada of Pitta.
notes: raktapītāsita may be 'red, yellow and dark' together or as alternatives; 'or' is used in the translation.
